title: Choose Hisaab's new look (round 2)
question: The new roll assigned Sivakasi Label. Keep it, take my pick or the alternate, take the standard look, or re-roll.

options.label: Sivakasi Label
options.thesis: Each screen's header is a printed label: a marigold field framed by a printed double rule, lettered bold, with flat spot inks and nothing glossy.
materials: flat spot inks on white board paper
options.viewport: A marigold label framed by a double rule fills the top with HISAAB lettered across it and 'You owe ₹10,532.09 overall' as one bold line; below on white, groups run as rows with a small peacock-blue kind tag (ROOM, FLAT, TRIP) and amounts on the right; a black Add expense button with marigold lettering sits at thumb height.
options.risk: Matchbox print can tip into kitsch, and marigold with black can read as a caution sign.

raised.raise: Destructive actions sit apart, separated by empty space, never beside a common button.
Rank comes from weight and case inside a short type scale, not from many sizes.
Everything snaps to one 8px grid; wide screens reflow by whole columns.
Settled payments are struck through in place; the one you are about to pay is ringed in marigold.
Columns never move; when an amount changes only that figure updates.

options.label: Last Page
options.lineage: The last pages of a hostel notebook where friends keep the hisaab
options.thesis: Hisaab the way friends already keep it: ballpoint-blue totals, double-underlined, struck through when paid.
options.viewport: A white page titled 'Your hisaab'; the overall total written large in ballpoint blue over a double underline; groups listed with amounts on the right, the settled Navratri group struck through; a blue Add expense button at the bottom.
options.risk: Every student knows this page, so it can tip into a school-notebook costume; the underlines must stay crisp, never cute.

options.label: Terminal Signs
options.thesis: Every screen shows the next step on a yellow sign band: who to pay, how much, which way.
options.viewport: A sticky yellow band reads 'You owe ₹10,532.09' with the amount at monumental size and '3 payments clear it' under it; groups below as band lines with amounts on the right; one black Add expense button.
options.case: Fuses cleanly and wins on clarity, since settle up becomes one next step at a time; loses on identification because it is airport signage, not friends' money.
options.risk: Yellow and black everywhere can feel like a warning sign.

options.label: Flip Board
options.thesis: Groups as departure rows, amounts flipping in fixed cells.
options.viewport: A black board of group rows with fixed columns.
options.risk: Reads as a control-room dashboard, not friends splitting money.
options.case: Fuses poorly for non-technical friends: dense caps in cells on a dark board.
options.kept: Fixed columns; only changed figures update.

options.label: Dev Console
options.thesis: Graphite panels split by hairline seams.
options.viewport: Tiled panels of groups and balances.
options.risk: Feels like a tool for programmers.
options.case: Fuses poorly: non-technical friends do not identify with a console.
options.kept: Destructive actions isolated by empty space.

options.label: Timetable Slides
options.thesis: Raked glass slides on a lit goldenrod bed, one type size.
options.viewport: A slanted rack of slides holding groups.
options.risk: Slanted containers fight a phone screen.
options.kept: Rank by weight and case, not size.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.thesis: Letterforms built on a visible construction grid.
options.viewport: Monumental grid-built numerals over a visible grid.
options.risk: A visible grid is decoration on a money screen.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no tie to friends or money.

options.label: Event Catalog
options.thesis: Hundreds of stamp-sized cells, circled in biro.
options.viewport: A packed grid of tiny cells.
options.kept: Done items struck through, the active one ringed.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What expense splitters ship, done very well: white list rows, avatars, a green and orange balance line.
canonCard.viewport: Overall balance as a line of text, groups as avatar rows, a floating Add expense button.
canonCard.risk: Looks like Splitwise by design, the same as every other app in the category.
